title: The Orin Relay Handbook
authorship: Original fictional fixture authored for Video Course Cards
purpose: Detect answers based on model priors instead of supplied evidence, and test deterministic citation and refusal behavior.

sections.heading: Luma states
sections.text: An Orin relay counts luma pulses in groups. Exactly three pulses place the relay in the amber state. Every other positive pulse count places it in the violet state. A relay with no observed pulse remains clear.

sections.heading: Packet routes
sections.text: The fictional Kestrel rule sends blue packets through the south channel and red packets through the north channel. Green packets are unsupported and must be refused rather than assigned a channel.

sections.heading: Merin gate
sections.text: A Merin gate may open only after a Tavo checksum is validated. Amber state alone never authorizes the gate. If checksum evidence is absent, the safe action is to keep the gate closed.

sections.heading: Noral drift
sections.text: One clockwise alignment reduces noral drift by two quants. One counterclockwise alignment increases it by one quant. These changes are applied in the order recorded by the relay.
